findings.claim: Scanner telemetry can become a disciplinary infrastructure when operational traces are retained and interpreted as individual quality or productivity evidence.
limits: No universal prevalence, named intent, liability or extra-record causation is inferred.

findings.claim: A public enforcement decision can recover the data and institutional purpose while still leaving the worker-level path from indicator to coaching, warning, restriction or dismissal incomplete.
limits: No universal prevalence, named intent, liability or extra-record causation is inferred.

findings.claim: The final judicial state must retain both the partial correction and the remaining sanction; reporting only the initial EUR 32 million or only the partial reversal would corrupt custody.
limits: No universal prevalence, named intent, liability or extra-record causation is inferred.

findings.claim: The record supports a pressure and proportionality analysis, not a finding that every scanner event caused an adverse action or that Amazon intended to purge dissent.
limits: No universal prevalence, named intent, liability or extra-record causation is inferred.

observations.claim: The CNIL decision described scanner-linked data processing that followed direct warehouse tasks at individual granularity and supported stock management, coaching, reassignment, planning and performance evaluation.
limits: Bounded to the named public record and stated jurisdiction.

observations.claim: The decision addressed 31-day access to individual productivity and quality details and found parts of the processing disproportionate or insufficiently minimized.
limits: Bounded to the named public record and stated jurisdiction.

observations.claim: The CNIL described constant, highly precise monitoring and pressure attached to scanner-based work and performance indicators.
limits: Bounded to the named public record and stated jurisdiction.

observations.claim: The 2023 decision imposed an initial public fine of EUR 32 million.
limits: Bounded to the named public record and stated jurisdiction.

observations.claim: On 23 December 2025 the Conseil d’État partially reformed the decision concerning three indicators and reduced the fine to EUR 15 million.
limits: Bounded to the named public record and stated jurisdiction.

observations.claim: The final judgment preserved other findings and required publication of the reformed result.
limits: Bounded to the named public record and stated jurisdiction.
